issues.description: The problem statement instructs that the SealSaloon should have a 'final Stock stock' initialized in the constructor (per-instance), but later explicitly states that the 'stock' attribute must be static (shared across all instances). The solution implements 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' (static, initialized at declaration). This contradiction about whether 'stock' is instance-level and initialized in the constructor or static (class-level) is ambiguous and can confuse students about how to declare and initialize the field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement. Either (A) require a static stock shared across all SealSaloon instances and state that it should be declared as 'private static final Stock stock' and initialized at declaration or in a static initializer, or (B) require a per-instance final stock and instruct students to initialize it in the no-argument constructor. Update the text that currently says to initialize stock in the constructor to match the choice.

issues.description: The UML and problem description specify a method checkOrderReady() with no parameters, but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) (i.e., it requires a boolean parameter). This changes the public signature compared to the specification and UML, creating a mismatch between the described API and the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent with the problem statement. Either change the solution to provide checkOrderReady() with no parameters (and move any debug-flag logic to a private helper or overload), or update the problem statement/UML to indicate a parameterized checkOrderReady(boolean) if that behaviour is intended. Prefer exposing the parameterless checkOrderReady() as the public API to match the specification.
